issues.description: Fix `text: '0deg'` for two-digit hues is non-obvious and relies on positional overlap
issues.detail: In tests like `oklch(from red l c 10)` → fix range [31, 32] with text '0deg', and `hsl(from red 10 s l)` → range [25, 26] text '0deg', the fix replaces only the second digit of '10' with '0deg' so the resulting string becomes '10deg'. This works but is confusing on read; a future change to fixer behavior could silently break it. A clearer fix would replace the trailing position with 'deg' (insertion) rather than overlapping the last digit.

issues.description: `isRelativeColor` only checks the literal token 'from'; no guard for malformed input
issues.detail: `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase() === 'from'` correctly identifies relative-color syntax including uppercase FROM, but if a function node accidentally lands at args[0] (e.g. a parser quirk), `.value` is the function name and the comparison silently returns false. This is acceptable but a brief comment noting why we trust postcss-value-parser to give a word here would help future maintainers.

issues.description: No test coverage for `color(from ... <colorspace> ...)` with hue channels
issues.detail: The CSS `color()` function with relative syntax has the form `color(from <color> <colorspace> r g b)` where args[1] is the colorspace identifier, not a channel. The patch does not address this because `color()` is not in HUE_FIRST_ARG_FUNCS or HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS, so it is correctly out of scope — but a brief test asserting `color(from red srgb 1 1 1)` is ignored would lock down the boundary.

issues.description: Channel-name tokens (`h`, `l`, `c`) bypass numeric validation implicitly
issues.detail: Accept cases like `oklch(from red l c h)` work because the downstream rule logic presumably ignores non-numeric word tokens. This is an implicit contract — if the rule ever begins flagging unknown tokens, these accept cases would regress. Worth a one-line comment in `findHue` or an explicit early-return for channel-identifier tokens.

issues.description: Nested relative-color cases (e.g. relative inside relative) are untested
issues.detail: The test `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` covers a non-relative inner function. A case like `oklch(from hsl(from red h s l) l c h)` would exercise the recursive walker's interaction with the new offset on both levels. Current logic should handle it (each function node is evaluated independently), but a test would prevent future regressions.

dissents.topic: Whether to also add a test for `color(from ...)` boundary

positions.position: Out of scope for this PR — the bug being fixed is hue-degree, and `color()` does not have a hue channel in the relevant function lists. Ship as-is.

Adding a one-line accept test for `color(from red srgb 1 1 1)` locks the boundary cheaply and protects against a future maintainer extending HUE_*_ARG_FUNCS without realizing the relative-color offset assumes args[1] is a color reference, not a colorspace.

dissents.topic: Whether the fix text overlap pattern (`'0deg'` replacing the digit '0') should be reworked

positions.position: The pattern obscures the actual transformation (insertion of 'deg' suffix) by overlapping the last digit. Refactor to an insertion-only fix with a clearer range/text relationship.
It matches existing fixer conventions in the file (line 130-ish for the non-relative cases use the same overlap trick). Stay consistent; refactor in a separate PR if at all.

review.summary: The fix is small, focused, and correctly addresses #8983: a single `isRelativeColor` check on args[0] adds a +2 offset to skip the `from <color>` prefix in CSS relative color syntax. Test coverage is solid — accept and reject cases cover both HUE_FIRST_ARG_FUNCS (`hsl`) and HUE_THIRD_ARG_FUNCS (`oklch`, `lch`), uppercase `FROM`, nested non-relative functions, and channel-identifier tokens. No correctness, performance, or data-structure concerns block merge. Minor nits: the fix-text overlap pattern is unusual but consistent with existing tests, and additional boundary tests (`color()` ignored, nested relative-in-relative) would be nice-to-have. Recommend merge as-is.
